name: FT-818ND
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not a Yaesu publication and not affiliated with Yaesu.
verified: Compiled from the Yaesu FT-818ND Operating Manual, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. The reset procedures could not be read and are left out.
specs: 100 kHz to 30 MHz, 50 to 54 MHz, 76 to 154 MHz, 420 to 470 MHz
160 through 6 m, plus 2 m and 70 cm, amateur bands only
SSB, CW, AM, FM and digital
6 W from external 13.8 V. Four steps: 6, 3.5, 2.5 and 1 W
The radio forces 2.5 W on the internal pack or eight AA cells
8 to 16 V DC, and the supply must hold 3 A
Two. Rear SO-239 and front BNC. Which one is live per band is a menu setting
Double conversion, first IF 68.33 MHz, second 455 kHz. 1 W of audio into 8 ohms
ACC jack, 8-pin mini DIN, shared with band data and cloning
keys: Press and hold one second to switch on or off.
Tap shows the current function row. Hold one second enters the menu.
Act on whatever function row is showing. There are eleven rows, scrolled with SEL after tapping F.
Detented. Tunes, selects memories, and picks the function row.
Switches between the VFO and the memory system.
Tap turns on the clarifier. Hold half a second turns on IF shift.
RF gain or squelch, whichever a menu item has assigned it to.
Green when the squelch opens, red on transmit.
quick: Memory write, memory check and skip, and channel naming.
Repeater shift, reverse, and the CTCSS encoder.
Transmit power, and what the meter shows.
VOX, break-in, and the internal keyer.
quick_right: tap F, then SEL to scroll
tasks: Tap F, SEL to the memory row, tap MW to enter memory check, SEL to the channel, then hold MW one second until the double beep.
Store the receive frequency as above. Set the transmit frequency in the VFO, tap MW, and while the channel number blinks, close the PTT while holding MW one second.
Tap V/M once. SEL picks the channel. V/M again returns to the VFO.
Tap SCN to start scanning upward. Tap again to stop.
Tap F, SEL to the VFO row, A/B to select VFO B, tune it, then tap SPL.
Tap F, SEL to the power row, tap PWR to step through the four levels.
Tap F, SEL to the repeater row. RPT selects minus then plus shift; hold RPT one second to reach the shift size. TON turns on the encoder; hold TON one second to reach the tone frequency.
notes: Six watts is the whole radio. Everything else about operating it follows from that: the antenna has to be better than the one you would get away with at a hundred watts.
The supply must hold 3 A even though the radio only makes six watts. A supply that sags will not just cut power, it will make the audio sound wrong on transmit.
Two antenna jacks, and a menu item decides which one is live per band. It is the first thing to check when a band appears to be dead.
On internal cells the radio drops to 2.5 W and does not ask. If your log shows six watts and you were on batteries, the log is wrong.
filters: Optional Collins CW filter, 300 Hz. The one that changes a crowded evening.
